h1: Stucco Repair in Calgary: Cracks, Patches, Bulges and Colour Matching
heroSub: See how independent Calgary stucco contractors scope a repair: what the crack is telling them, whether a patch will hold, and when a wall needs more than a patch. Call (403) 555-0148 for a no-obligation quote.
introHtml:
Stucco repair in Calgary starts with a diagnosis, not a trowel. A hairline crack, a patch of hail pocking, a bulge over the garage and a hollow spot beside a window can look alike from the driveway and need very different work. This page walks through how an independent stucco contractor sorts them, what a patch can and cannot do, and what Calgary firms publish for prices.

Sandstone Stucco Co is an advertising service paid by independent contractors. It puts homeowners in Calgary, Airdrie, Chestermere, Cochrane and Okotoks in touch with them, and the contractor who quotes your job contracts directly with you. This site does no stucco work itself. Call (403) 555-0148 and describe the wall, or see the stucco repair cost guide for more figures.

features.title: Hairline versus structural cracks
features.desc: Imasco, a stucco manufacturer, says some cracking is inherent to portland cement and is not a reflection of product quality. Ask the contractor where the crack starts, how wide it is and whether it has moved.

features.title: Patches and holes
features.desc: Martini Stone Masonry lists one back-wall repair as flashing, paper, mesh, two coats of mortar and a matched texture. Calgary Parging lists small patch repairs at $550 to $1,125 before GST.

features.title: Bulges and delamination
features.desc: Calgary Parging lists bulge repair, such as above a garage, at $1,450 to $3,000 before GST. Calgary Stucco and Slate notes that nobody can name the full extent of water damage until the wall is opened up.

features.title: Windows, doors and the base of the wall
features.desc: Martini Stone Masonry says temperature movement opens 3 to 8 mm gaps where stucco meets frames, and that piled snow softens the lowest 12 to 18 inches of a wall. Calgary Parging lists window and door repairs at $975 to $3,000 before GST.

features.title: Colour and texture match
features.desc: Imasco, a stucco manufacturer, says colour can vary with weather, texture, job conditions and method of application. Ask the contractor how close a patch will get before work starts.

features.title: Repair or recoat
features.desc: Total Exteriors, a Calgary contractor, suggests repair when damage is localized and moisture is minimal. The call is the contractor's, made after seeing your wall.

sections.heading: How a stucco repair is scoped
sections.html:
A useful quote describes the wall, not just the price. Expect the contractor to look at cracks, soft or spongy areas, peeling or bubbling, and how water leaves the roof and gutters. Weststar Wall Systems lists soft or spongy areas and peeling or bubbling as warning signs, and Calgary Parging said in 2024 that over 30% of its residential repairs address water damage from incorrectly installed gutters, eaves or flashing.

When you compare written quotes, check that each one names the same things:

  • The area and elevation being repaired, with rough dimensions
  • How deep the repair goes: a surface patch, or back to the paper and mesh
  • Whether scaffolding is needed for upper-storey or peaked sections
  • How the colour and texture will be matched
  • Whether damaged sheathing is priced now or held as an allowance if found
  • Whether the figure is incl. or ex GST (5%)
  • How many visits the cure and finish coats take

Calgary Parging lists colour match as adding $230 to $575, scaffolding for upper-storey or peaked sections at typically $4,000 to $12,900, and water-damaged sheathing or board at $575 to $2,300 or more, all before GST. Those are one firm's published figures, not a Calgary price. The contractor quotes your job after seeing it.

sections.heading: When a patch is enough and when a wall needs a recoat
sections.html:
A patch suits damage that is localized on a wall that is otherwise sound. Total Exteriors says repair fits when the damage is localized, moisture intrusion is minimal and has not spread, and the majority of the stucco is structurally sound. It lists widespread or structural damage, extensive moisture problems and stucco beyond its natural lifespan as the cases for replacement.

Two firms will not always agree on where that line falls, and lifespan figures vary from firm to firm, so treat any single number as that firm's view. Alberta.ca advises getting written estimates from more than one business. Ask each contractor to explain in writing why they chose a patch or a recoat.

For whole-wall work, read about re-stucco in Calgary. For pocked or cracked stucco after a storm, or bird holes, see hail and woodpecker stucco damage. Foundation coating is a separate job, covered on the parging page.

sections.heading: Why a patch shows, and how contractors try to hide it
sections.html:
Imasco says colour variations may occur due to weather, texture, job conditions and method of application, and advises buying the same colour batch number for the complete job. It also says adding water while floating or trowelling will disturb the colour, and that variation is more noticeable in darker colours.

Age matters as much as batch. Calgary Parging says a cement finish and an acrylic finish age and weather differently. On heavily weathered or discontinued finishes it says it will tell you upfront if a perfect match is not achievable, and offer to refinish a full elevation instead. Martini Stone Masonry says matching an aged finish takes trial batches.

Ask any contractor how they plan to match your wall and whether a full-elevation refinish is on the table if the patch will not blend. Calgary Parging lists colour matching as an add-on of $230 to $575 before GST, so get it written into the quote.

sections.heading: Season, curing and cold-weather limits
sections.html:
Cement-based stucco needs warmth to cure. Imasco's traditional stucco guide specification says to do no stucco work when air and substrate temperatures are below 4°C or above 38°C for 24 hours before, during and after application, and to moist cure for a minimum of 48 hours. Its cement finish data sheet says the finish coat may go on after a minimum of 7 days in ideal conditions.

ADEX, another manufacturer, calls for ambient and surface temperatures at or above 5°C for a minimum of 24 hours for its base coat. It also says additives such as antifreeze or accelerators are strictly forbidden. Calgary Parging puts the best season at April through October and says off-season repairs need heated hoarding.

Durations differ by firm and by job. Calgary Parging says most repairs take 1 to 3 days depending on scope and weather. Calgary Stucco and Slate says some repairs take two trips and some up to four, with up to weeks in between so each layer cures. In winter, ask the contractor what can be done now, what needs a heated enclosure and what should wait for spring.

faq.q: How much does stucco crack or patch repair cost in Calgary?
faq.a: Firms publish different figures, so treat each as that firm's own. Calgary Parging lists small patch repairs at $550 to $1,125 and medium repairs at $1,250 to $2,650, before 5% GST. Dynamic Painting Inc. lists small hairline crack repair at $800 to $1,500 (April 2026, GST not stated). The contractor quotes your job after seeing the wall.

faq.q: What does a bulge or damage around a window cost to repair?
faq.a: Calgary Parging lists bulge repair, such as above a garage, at $1,450 to $3,000 and repairs around windows or doors at $975 to $3,000, both before GST. It lists scaffolding for upper-storey or peaked sections separately at typically $4,000 to $12,900 ex GST. Water-damaged sheathing found once the wall is open adds $575 to $2,300 or more ex GST on the same firm's list.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for stucco repair in Calgary?
faq.a: The City of Calgary says most repair or replacement work does not need a development or building permit, and its renovations page allows replacing exterior cladding with a similar material. Siding with a different material needs a building permit, and changing window or door openings needs development and building permits. Confirm your project with the City through 311. The City also says contractors must hold a valid City of Calgary business licence, which you can check by calling 311.

faq.q: Can stucco be repaired in winter?
faq.a: Manufacturers set the limits. Imasco says no stucco work below 4°C for 24 hours before, during and after application, and ADEX asks for 5°C or above for at least 24 hours. Calgary Parging says off-season repairs need heated hoarding. Ask the contractor whether they will hoard and heat the wall or schedule the work for spring.

faq.q: My stucco has hail damage. What should I do first?
faq.a: The Insurance Bureau of Canada says hail damage is typically covered by home insurance policies, so check your own policy. The City of Calgary advises contacting your home insurance provider before doing any repair work. IBC's steps include photographing the damage, calling your insurer and keeping receipts. A contractor can give you a written repair estimate to pass to your insurer; you deal with the insurer yourself, and this site does not handle claims.
